successors.note: Ceded by Sweden to Denmark at Kiel (14 January 1814) in exchange for Norway, then transferred to Prussia by the Congress of Vienna treaties (4 June with Denmark, 7 June with Sweden, 1815); the infobox gives the hand-over as 23 October 1815. The southern part went to Prussia in 1720 and Wismar to Mecklenburg-Schwerin in 1803.

ledger.note: 6 July 1630: Gustavus Adolphus lands on Usedom and Swedish Pomerania begins. He 'landed near Peenemünde on Usedom with about 13,000 troops' and took Stettin on 9 July; the infobox dates the start to the Treaty of Stettin of 10 July 1630 (signed 4 September N.S., predated).

region.text: the whole Duchy of Pomerania, Hither and Farther Pomerania, as the duchy-of-pomerania dossier draws it

ledger.note: 1630: Sweden holds the duchy under the Treaty of Stettin. Pomerania owed 100,000 talers a year and four Swedish garrisons; 'Sweden gained absolute control over the duchy's military affairs. The dukes, nobles, and towns kept political and ecclesiastical power'; imperial forces were cleared in 1631 (Greifswald surrendered 16 June 1631). The duchy-of-pomerania dossier records the same as an occupation.

region.text: the whole Duchy of Pomerania, Hither and Farther Pomerania, as the duchy-of-pomerania dossier draws it

ledger.note: 10 March 1637: Bogislaw XIV dies, the last of his house, and the occupation of the duchy becomes Swedish administration. 'Bogislaw XIV died without issue.'

region.text: the whole Duchy of Pomerania, Hither and Farther Pomerania, as the duchy-of-pomerania dossier draws it

ledger.note: 1637-1638: the Swedes administer the whole duchy. On 24 February 1637 the Pomeranian councillors decided the 1634 constitution should stand if the duke died, and 'Sweden approved; Brandenburg rejected'; governors were appointed on 2 May 1638 and 'by the end of 1638' Johan Banér 'was general governor of the whole duchy'. Brandenburg's claim rested on the treaties of Pyritz (1493) and Grimnitz (1529).

region.text: Western Pomerania (Vorpommern) with Rügen and Usedom, from the Recknitz to the Oder

ledger.note: 24/25 October 1637: imperial forces under von Bredow enter Western Pomerania. The emperor granted the duchy to Brandenburg as a fief, accepted by the nobility on 26 January 1638; Banér attacked the imperial forces on 28 July 1638.

ledger.note: 24 October 1648: the Peace of Westphalia leaves Farther Pomerania to Brandenburg. 'Western Pomerania remained with Sweden; Farther Pomerania became a Brandenburg fief.' Brandenburg also got Kammin, Magdeburg, Halberstadt and Minden as compensation (Westphalia page).

ledger.note: 24 October 1648: Sweden receives Wismar. 'Sweden received Western Pomerania, which became Swedish Pomerania, along with Wismar'; the Mecklenburg dukes were to cede Wismar (Sweden read the clause as covering all Mecklenburg port tolls). The Wismar page: 'part of Sweden from 1648 until 1803'.

region.text: Western Pomerania (Vorpommern) with Rügen and Usedom, from the Recknitz to the Oder

ledger.note: 4 May 1653: the Treaty of Stettin settles the border with Brandenburg 'in Sweden's favour'. The Westphalia page: the treaty 'did not settle the Swedish-Brandenburgian border in Pomerania'.
1675: Danish forces capture Wismar in the Scanian War. 'The town was besieged and captured by Danish forces in 1675.'

1679: Wismar back under Sweden. The Wismar page does not say when Denmark gave it up; the year follows the Swedish Pomerania page's 1679 restoration of Sweden's German territories at Saint-Germain-en-Laye (bridging).

notes: Type colony: a dominion of the Swedish crown that was also an imperial fief ('remained part of the Holy Roman Empire', making the Swedish rulers imperial princes). Cliopatria draws it inside its Swedish Empire shapes (1632-1635 and 1648-1814); the renderer should draw it as a tint of Sweden. Wismar is included (Peace of Westphalia page; it was a separate Swedish dominion, 'Swedish Wismar'). Five pages opened. Not settled: the Brandenburg conquests of 1675-1679 in Pomerania (not dated on the opened pages), Stettin's loss to Russia/Prussia in 1713 (not on the pages; the 1720 treaty is dated), the Great Northern War page's 1716 Wismar surrender against the Wismar page's continuous Swedish rule, whether Denmark's 1715 occupation covered Wismar. The shapes use polygons clipped to Mecklenburg-Vorpommern and West Pomeranian because the gazetteer lacks Rügen, Usedom, Wolin, Greifswald, Wolgast and Gartz; the Peene and Oder lines are approximate. 1814: the Treaty of Kiel is a rename event only. The Duchy of Pomerania dossier names this occupier 'swedish-empire'; the counterpart here is the duchy, so the pair needs reconciling by the orchestrator.
